steps.claim: A semantic call must have an invocation-path element identified by its constructor expansion occurrence, and repeated calls must have distinct paths. Fixed lproc binding instances also retain distinct identities even when values agree; §9.2 says invocation paths distinguish their uses.

The serialized schedule element contains only symbol, source point and iteration; the certificate context key adds oracle step/phase. K49 removes lift.call sites from the chain. Neither schema carries a constructor call occurrence or a fixed-binding key, and generated selects a callee-local leaf ordinal, not its caller occurrence.

Take a one-bit identity-function oracle G with F=4, a sufficient token and a covering inverse-pair certificate. One action row qinplace @G @G tk x generates two calls of G. For a corresponding leaf of source row q in G, both chains are [(A, entry:0, []), (G, q, [])], with identical nested step, phase and generated ordinal. There are no source qloops to distinguish iteration. Assigning both this source path obeys §11 but violates §11.1 distinctness; inserting a constructor occurrence distinguishes them but requires an unspecified encoding and validation rule outside the printed schema. This is a collision before hashing.
steps.by: witness:"qinplace @G @G tk x"; clause:ISA-4.5-P5; clause:ISA-11.1-P9; clause:ISA-11.1-P29

steps.claim: Q14 creates a second instance of the same problem: two lift.call sites forwarding distinct root token positions to the same lproc create distinct row instances. At one padded outer step, both instances expand their nested call row, but their source symbol/point, iteration, step and phase coincide after K49 removes lift.call. Their nested budgets and classical arguments can differ. Thus this is not only redundant identity-oracle execution; certificate contexts with different resolved invocations can have the same prescribed key.
steps.by: witness:"lift.call @f (x) (ta) () (); lift.call @f (x) (tb) () ()", with f containing a lift.oracle_call and ta/tb resolving to different tuples; clause:ISA-3.7-P5; clause:ISA-3.7-P6; clause:ISA-9.2-P1.S3; clause:ISA-11-P5.S2

steps.claim: The new occurrence-distinctness obligation and the serialized path contract cannot both be implemented as written. A source-point consumer aliases these contexts, while an occurrence-path consumer needs private fields or synthetic points, producing incompatible schedule validation and certificate-context enumeration. This is S0 contract interoperability, not a request for a proof or an optimization.

blocking.fix: In §11 and §12.1 state: "Every invocation edge identifies the source call point, the containing fixed-binding instance (the §3.7 integer binding key, or [] outside an lproc instance), and the zero-based semantic-call occurrence within that source row expansion. Occurrences are numbered in instantiated constructor traversal order before descending into callees, independently of leaf ordinals; inverse traversal retains the forward occurrence number. These components are part of the concrete invocation chain and context key." Add instance and call_index selectors to path elements, allowing * and treating omission as *, and validate concrete values against the source and bound library; retain the existing lexicographic specificity rule, so newly overlapping equal-specificity entries still tie. Give qinplace @G @G call_index 0 and 1 and distinct context keys; give the two lproc instances their distinct positional binding keys. Update §9.2-P1 and K49 to say once per fixed row instance per step. Declare dependencies on ISA-3.7-P5/P6, ISA-9.2-P1.S3, ISA-11.1-P9 and ISA-12.1-P11. An alternative is an explicitly specified synthetic-point encoding carrying the same two components; prefer explicit fields because source points remain independently checkable. Neither alternative restores dynamic lift.call histories.

steps.claim: The specification does not identify a realization-independent carrier against which a cleanup-kind entry selects one decision for a whole cleanup. The progress record explicitly carries INV-5 gap 8 as b-isa-spec-23g.

steps.claim: For d=qcopy s followed by quncopy s d, reverse emits the inverse copy and release, whereas recompute allocates a fresh bundle, computes a copy, XORs, uncomputes and releases. Matching cleanup against each generated leaf can select different realizations for one cleanup; matching only its first realized leaf makes the carrier depend on the choice it is supposed to determine.
steps.by: witness:"d = qcopy s; quncopy s d", scheduled as reverse versus recompute; clause:ISA-6.4-P1.S1; clause:ISA-11-P6.S6
